title: SMART Guidelines KG L2 classes
description: The classes an L2 (DAK) knowledge-graph node can be: the kit, its personas, scenarios, processes, decisions, indicators and requirements. smart-base document kinds and the recommendation scenarios name these as `sgkg-l2#<code>`. Taken on 2026-10-23 from litlfred/smart-kg at 66a9b1393fd7, which had been pinned since 2026-10-02 (bean pebe). smart-kg is deprecated (owner, 2026-10-16), so smart-base owns this list now: edit it here, not upstream.

source.note: litlfred/smart-kg ontology/l2/l2.json at 66a9b1393fd7, the `classes` array: id, name, note and iri.

codes.label: Digital Adaptation Kit
codes.definition: The kit itself. Properties are exactly the metadata fields DAK.fsh declares and dak.json carries -- no more, so that a dak node can be produced from a real file without anything being invented.

codes.label: Generic Persona
codes.definition: DAK component 2. Grounded in GenericPersona.fsh -- title, id, description, otherNames, iscoCode bound to ISCO08ValueSet -- and in the 22 committed ActorDefinition instances that carry name, title, type and description. The two disagree about where ISCO lives, which the properties record rather than smooth over.

codes.label: User Scenario
codes.definition: DAK component 3. A narrative describing how personas interact. Carries `personas 0..* id`, which is the only structured link between the narrative layer and the personas it names.

codes.label: Business Process Workflow
codes.definition: DAK component 4. NOT the BPMN file -- the component that points at one. `source 1..1 uri` is that pointer, and the BPMN's interior is the l2-bpmn subgraph, reached through the external-artifact this sourcedFrom targets.

codes.label: Task Entry
codes.definition: One entry of BusinessProcessWorkflow's `task 0..*` backbone: identifier, name, description. A node rather than a property because the same task is also drawn in the BPMN file, and the two lists have to be joinable to be checkable against each other.

codes.label: Core Data Element
codes.definition: DAK component 5. CoreDataElement.fsh calls itself "the ONE EXCEPTION to allowing FHIR R4 models into the DAK LMs": `type` is one of valueset | codesystem | conceptmap | logicalmodel and `canonical 1..1 uri` points at it. The canonical is recorded; nothing inside it is copied, because FHIR is its own query layer.

codes.label: Decision-Support Logic
codes.definition: DAK component 6. The whole model is an id, an optional description and `source 1..1 uri` to a DMN file. Nothing about the decision itself -- which is the gap the l2-dmn subgraph fills.

codes.label: Scheduling Logic
codes.definition: When an intervention is due, as a DAK component. NOT declared by DAK.fsh -- it is added here because the published SOP lists Scheduling Logic as an active L2 input (spreadsheets under input/scheduling-logic), WHO's ArchiMate model declares it a BusinessObject realised by PlanDefinition, and l1:schedule and l1:schedule-entry had no L2 component to reach. Note that the SOP's own L3 row for scheduling is present but HTML-commented-out and there is no l3_schedulinglogic.md page, so WHO has drafted the mapping and not activated it; the L3 edge is licensed here as a deliberate departure, recorded rather than hidden.

codes.label: Program Indicator
codes.definition: DAK component 7. Named program-indicator and not `indicator` because L1 already declares an `indicator` -- one normatively defined in a publication. They are different things: this is the DAK's operational measure, and `derivedFrom` is how it points at the normative one. Collapsing them would silently merge a WHO definition with a country's implementation of it.

codes.label: Functional Requirement
codes.definition: DAK component 8, first half. The as-a/I-want/so-that shape: `activity`, `capability[x]`, `benefit[x]`, and `actor 0..* Reference(SGActor)`. The 41 committed instances use the R5 SGRequirements profile rather than this logical model, so a real instance carries `statement` entries and a userstory extension; both shapes are accommodated and `profile` records which was read.

codes.label: Non-Functional Requirement
codes.definition: DAK component 8, second half. `requirement 1..1 markdown`, an optional category and classification codings. Kept separate from the functional half because the fields genuinely differ -- a non-functional requirement has no actor and no benefit.

codes.label: Requirement Statement
codes.definition: One numbered, labelled statement inside a requirement, with a conformance verb. A node rather than a property because conformance is queried across a whole DAK -- 'every SHALL in this kit, and what fulfils it' is the question requirements exist to answer.

codes.label: Test Scenario
codes.definition: DAK component 9. `feature 1..1 uri` to a Gherkin feature file, plus an optional description. The feature file's interior is not modelled: no DAK in this estate ships one yet, so a subgraph for it would have no instance to check it against.
